ticket.subject: Refunds working on new payments but rejected on older ones
ticket.body: Our ops team processes returns in a weekly sweep and about a third of them started bouncing back this month. Anything charged recently refunds fine. The older ones come back 400 with PAY_4013 and no other detail in the response. Example is pay_3Kd91xR2, request id req_8812fa04. We are on v3 across the board. I checked the amounts and they are well under what we took, and the payments show as captured, so I do not think it is an amount problem. Is there some cutoff on how far back we can go, or did something change on your side recently that we missed?

outputs.reference_answer: In v3 a payment can be refunded up to 90 days after capture on POST /v3/payments/{id}/refund. A refund attempted after that window returns PAY_4013, which is about the time window only and never about the amount, which would be PAY_4012. The older payments in the weekly sweep are past the 90 day mark, so nothing changed recently. Compare captured_at from GET /v3/payments/{id} against the 90 day window and settle anything outside it outside the payments API.

ticket.subject: Nightly cancellation job started 404ing after version upgrade
ticket.body: We finished cutting over from the older API last week. Since then our nightly job that cancels stale authorizations logs 404 on every single call. Nothing else changed, same auth header, same payment ids that we can still fetch fine with a GET. The path we hit is /v3/payments/{id}/void and it just returns not found, no error code in the body at all. If I fetch the same payment it comes back with status authorized so the id is definitely real. Did that route move, or do we need a flag turned on for our account?

outputs.reference_answer: The void route is removed in v3, so /v3/payments/{id}/void is no longer served and returns 404 for every request. Use POST /v3/payments/{id}/reversal instead, which releases an authorization that has not been captured and frees the held funds. The old call maps over directly, with the same POST method, the payment id in the same path position, and the optional amount and reason fields carried over unchanged. Reversal emits the payment.reversed event, the same event the old void call emitted. If a payment was already captured, reversal returns PAY_4023 and you should call refund instead.

ticket.subject: Need one missed notification re-sent to a single endpoint only
ticket.body: Our fraud service was offline for roughly 20 minutes yesterday during a deploy and it missed a notification in that window. Everything before and after came through fine. We have three receivers registered and the other two got that same notification without any problem. I want you to push that one message to the fraud service again and only to that one. What I do not want is the other two receivers getting a second copy, because our reconciliation job is not tolerant of that and will double count. Delivery id on the failed one is whd_88fLz2. What is the correct way to do this?

outputs.reference_answer: Use POST /v3/webhooks/deliveries/{id}/retry with the failed delivery id whd_88fLz2. In v3 that route re-sends one failed delivery to one endpoint, and the new attempt is appended to the same delivery record rather than creating a new one. Do not use /v3/webhooks/events/{id}/replay, because replay re-emits the event to all currently active endpoints and creates a delivery for each, which is exactly the duplicate copy you want to avoid. Retry works only on a delivery whose status is failed, which happens after 5 attempts return WHK_4100. v3 also adds an optional backoff field of immediate, linear, or exponential, defaulting to exponential.

ticket.subject: Sandbox keeps returning 429 while production is completely fine
ticket.body: Running our integration suite against sandbox and it falls over constantly with 429 responses about half way through. The exact same suite pointed at production never sees a single one. It is not a huge amount of traffic, maybe a few hundred calls over a couple of minutes with some parallelism. My assumption is our sandbox account is broken or has been throttled for some reason, since a test environment being stricter than prod makes no sense to me. Can someone check if there is something wrong with the key? Sample request id is req_44b1c9de.

outputs.reference_answer: Nothing is wrong with the key, sandbox is deliberately stricter than production. The sandbox limit is 30 requests per minute in both v2 and v3, while production allows 600 requests per minute in v3 and 60 in v2, so the same traffic that passes in production returns RATE_LIMITED with HTTP 429 in sandbox. Honor the Retry-After response header before retrying, and lower concurrency against sandbox to stay under 30 requests per minute.

ticket.subject: Receipt lookups all 404 since we moved to the new API version
ticket.body: We generate customer statements every morning and the job died the first morning after our upgrade. The part that pulls the receipt for each charge now gets a 404 back on every single charge, including ones we successfully pulled receipts for the week before. The call we make is GET /v3/payments/{id}/receipt with pay_3Kd91xR2 as the id. The payment itself still fetches fine and shows as captured, so the id is good and our key is good. Nothing in the 404 body tells us anything. Was this endpoint retired, and if so where do we read the receipt fields like receipt_number and line_items now?

outputs.reference_answer: The receipt route is removed in v3, so GET /v3/payments/{id}/receipt is no longer served and returns 404 for every request. Fetch the receipt through the payment instead with GET /v3/payments/{id}?expand=receipt, which inlines the full receipt object so one call returns both the payment and its receipt. Everything the old response returned at the top level now sits under the receipt key with the same field names, including receipt_number, issued_at, amount_settled, and line_items, so read them one level deeper. A receipt exists only after the payment has settled, so an uncaptured payment returns a null receipt, and an unknown payment id returns PAY_4001.

ticket.subject: Receiver health check script broke after the upgrade, 404 on every run
ticket.body: We run a small script every morning that pokes all of our registered receivers at once to confirm they are up before the payment traffic starts. Since we moved to the new version it just returns 404 and does nothing. It posts to /v3/webhooks/ping with an empty body and that is the whole script, one call, no ids involved. Our receivers themselves are fine and are taking real traffic normally. Auth is unchanged and other calls on the same key work. Has this been retired, and if so how do we get the same all receivers check working again without waiting for real traffic to prove it?

outputs.reference_answer: The ping route is removed in v3, so POST /v3/webhooks/ping returns 404 for every account. Use POST /v3/webhooks/endpoints/{id}/test instead and fan the check out yourself, listing your endpoints with GET /v3/webhooks/endpoints and calling the test route once per endpoint id. Each call sends one synthetic test event to one endpoint and returns the delivery row for that attempt, so a broken receiver is identified by the call that failed rather than by reading delivery rows afterwards. The test route also accepts an optional event_type field, which ping never had, and an unknown endpoint id returns WHK_4004. Each synthetic event is signed with the per-endpoint secret returned once when that endpoint was created.

ticket.subject: Some charges refuse to settle with a 402 PAY_4030 while most go through
ticket.body: About one in six of our authorizations will not settle. When our settlement worker tries to take the money it comes back 402 with PAY_4030 and no further explanation. The rest of the batch on the same run settles normally. The failing ones are all consumer cards on European issuers if that matters, and they all show status requires_action when we fetch them. We are on v3. Retrying the same call later does not help, it fails the same way every time. Sample payment is pay_3Kd91xR2. What is different about these payments and what should the worker do when it sees that code?

outputs.reference_answer: Those payments still need 3DS authentication before money can move. In v3 POST /v3/payments/{id}/capture returns 402 PAY_4030 for a payment that has not completed the authentication step, and retrying capture will keep failing. Call POST /v3/payments/{id}/confirm first, which is new in v3 and moves no money, passing return_url so the cardholder can be returned after the challenge. Once authentication_status comes back succeeded, capture the payment. Confirm emits payment.confirmed and the later capture emits payment.captured.

ticket.subject: Cannot undo a charge, getting 422 PAY_4023 back
ticket.body: A customer disputed a charge this morning and our agent tried to undo it through our internal tool. The call our tool makes to release the money came back 422 with PAY_4023 and the money is still gone from the customer account. The payment is pay_3Kd91xR2, it was taken four days ago and shows status captured. The same tool works fine when an agent cancels something on the same day it was authorized, so I think the difference is how long we waited. We are on v3. Is there a different call we should be making once the money has actually moved?

outputs.reference_answer: Reversal only releases an authorization that was never captured, so in v3 POST /v3/payments/{id}/reversal on a payment that was already captured returns 422 PAY_4023. Because pay_3Kd91xR2 is captured, call POST /v3/payments/{id}/refund instead to return the settled money. In v3 a payment can be refunded up to 90 days after capture, and after that the refund returns PAY_4013. A refund sent before the capture settles and the payment.captured event is emitted returns PAY_4022, so wait for that event first.

ticket.subject: Paging through charges is stuck on page one after the upgrade
ticket.body: Our reconciliation job walks every charge from the previous day and it now only ever sees the first 20 rows. The way it was written it read a count field off the response, divided by the page size and looped from there, and that field is simply not in the payload any more so the loop never runs a second time. The response does have two fields we were not reading before, one looks like an opaque string and one is a boolean. We upgraded to v3 last week and nothing else in the job changed. What is the right way to walk the full result set now, and is there still any way to know how many rows match before we start?

outputs.reference_answer: In v3 GET /v3/payments uses cursor pagination instead of offset pagination. Pass cursor and limit as query parameters, then follow next_cursor from each response until has_more is false, at which point next_cursor is null. There is no total_count field in v3, so you cannot compute a page count up front and should not try. v2 GET /v2/payments used offset pagination with offset and limit and returned total_count in the response. The maximum limit is 100 in both versions.

ticket.subject: Which notification confirms a refund, and occasional 422 right after taking payment
ticket.body: Two things on the same flow. First, when we issue a refund our ledger service needs to hear about it from the notification stream rather than from the API response, so which message type should we be listening for? We already consume the capture one. Second, in our same day return path we take the money and then refund it a few seconds later if the customer backs out, and maybe one in twenty of those comes back 422 with PAY_4022. Retrying the identical call a minute later works every time. Example payment is pay_3Kd91xR2. Is that a race on our side or yours?

outputs.reference_answer: Listen for the payment.refunded webhook event, which POST /v3/payments/{id}/refund emits on a successful refund and which appears in the v3 event type list returned by GET /v3/webhooks/events alongside payment.created, payment.confirmed, payment.captured, payment.reversed and payment.failed. The 422 is not a race on your side. In v3, refunding before the capture has settled and the payment.captured event has been emitted returns PAY_4022, which means the payment status does not yet permit the operation. Poll GET /v3/payments/{id} until status is captured, or wait for the payment.captured event, then send the refund. That is why the same call succeeds a minute later.

ticket.subject: Backlog of failed notifications after an outage, retrying makes it worse
ticket.body: We had a bad afternoon. One of our receivers sat behind a load balancer returning 502s for about 90 minutes during a certificate rollout. In that window a few hundred notifications piled up against it. They now show as failed in the delivery listing after several attempts each, and what we captured on the last attempt was WHK_4100. The receiver is healthy again and returns 200 to a manual curl. Where it gets ugly is that when I looped through the failed ones and fired retries back to back, the receiver started timing out again and a chunk of them flipped straight back to failed. So now I am scared to touch it. I need this backlog delivered without knocking the thing over a second time, and I do not want the other two receivers on the account picking up duplicates. Endpoint is whe_71bQm4, one example is whd_88fLz2. What is the sane way to drain this?

outputs.reference_answer: Drain the backlog with POST /v3/webhooks/deliveries/{id}/retry, one call per failed delivery, and set the v3 backoff field rather than firing them back to back. In v3 backoff is one of immediate, linear or exponential and defaults to exponential, so leaving it unset or choosing linear spaces the attempts out instead of hammering the receiver. WHK_4100 means the endpoint was unreachable after 5 attempts and the delivery was marked failed, which is exactly the state retry works on. Retry re-sends ONE failed delivery to ONE endpoint and appends the attempt to the same delivery record, so your other two receivers see nothing. Do not use POST /v3/webhooks/events/{id}/replay here, because replay re-emits the event to ALL currently active endpoints and creates new deliveries, which is how you would get duplicates on the other two.

ticket.subject: Every incoming notification fails verification after upgrade
ticket.body: Upgraded to the new version over the weekend and recreated all four of our receiver registrations from scratch as part of it. Since then not one incoming message passes our verification check. We log WHK_4220 against every single one. The thing that is bugging me is that our verification code has not been touched in over a year, and it worked perfectly the day before the cutover. Same raw body handling, same comparison, same value pulled from our secrets store that we have always used. Endpoint whe_71bQm4 if you want to look. Is something wrong with how the signature is being generated on your side after the upgrade?

outputs.reference_answer: Nothing is wrong with the signature generation, the secret you verify against changed with the version. In v2 signatures were computed with the account-level signing secret shared by every endpoint, which is the value sitting in your secrets store. In v3 every delivery listed by GET /v3/webhooks/deliveries is signed with the per-endpoint secret, and the signing key is returned exactly once in the POST /v3/webhooks/endpoints create response and never again. WHK_4220 is a signature mismatch, so your old account secret can no longer verify anything. Because you recreated all four endpoints, you need the signing_key from each create response, and if it was not stored you must delete the endpoint and create it again with a fresh secret. Also compute the signature over the exact raw body before any parsing.

ticket.subject: Two listings disagree by about 3x, are we being notified twice
ticket.body: Doing month end reconciliation and the numbers do not line up. For the same window one listing gives me roughly 1,900 rows and the other gives me a bit over 5,600. I pulled a single captured payment out of the noisy one and it shows up five separate times with the same payment id, different ids on the rows themselves, and an attempt counter that climbs 1 through 5. Ops is now convinced we are notifying our downstream three times over and wants me to dedupe on the payment id before anything is booked. That feels wrong to me but I cannot explain the gap. Example payment is pay_3Kd91xR2, one of the repeated rows is whd_88fLz2. Which of these two is the source of truth for how many things actually happened?

outputs.reference_answer: You are not being notified three times over, you are comparing two different things. GET /v3/webhooks/events returns one row per event that happened in the account, so that is the source of truth for how many things occurred. GET /v3/webhooks/deliveries returns one row per HTTP attempt made to send one event to one endpoint, so one event usually has many delivery rows, one per active endpoint and one more per retried attempt. The climbing attempt counter you saw is those attempts on one delivery, and a delivery is marked failed after 5 attempts with WHK_4100. Reconcile against the events listing, and use the deliveries listing with the event_id filter only when you want to audit what was actually sent.

ticket.subject: Which message means the cardholder finished the challenge vs money actually moved, plus 402s
ticket.body: Our risk team and our ledger team want different signals and I keep wiring them to the same one. Risk wants to know the moment the cardholder has cleared the step up challenge on their phone. Ledger only cares about the point where funds are genuinely taken. Right now both are subscribed to the same message type and risk is complaining they hear about it far too late. Separately, on the cards that go through the challenge we get a 402 with PAY_4030 when we take the money on our usual schedule. When support walks that customer through the challenge again and we re run the same call afterwards it goes through. Feels like we are doing these two steps in the wrong order. Example is pay_3Kd91xR2.

outputs.reference_answer: These are two separate steps in v3. POST /v3/payments/{id}/confirm is the 3DS authentication step, it moves no money, and it emits payment.confirmed, which is the signal your risk team wants and which is new in v3. POST /v3/payments/{id}/capture is what moves the money on an already authenticated authorization, and it emits payment.captured once the capture settles, which is the ledger signal. The 402 with PAY_4030 means the payment still needs authentication, so capture is being called before confirm. Call confirm first, wait for authentication to succeed, then capture. Note that confirm does not exist in v2, where authentication failures surface at capture time instead.

ticket.subject: Getting 429s while clearing a notification backlog, how hard can we push
ticket.body: We have about 4,000 stuck notifications to push through after a receiver outage last night and I wrote a small worker with 20 threads to work the list. It ran fine for maybe ninety seconds and then everything started coming back 429. I dialled it down to 10 threads and still got them, just less often. What is throwing me is that the same worker against our test account fell over almost immediately, way faster than production did, so I cannot even rehearse the run safely. There is a header on the 429 responses that we are currently ignoring. I need a number I can size the worker against, and I would rather not sit here guessing. This is on the new API version if that matters.

outputs.reference_answer: On v3 the limit is 600 requests per minute in production and 30 requests per minute in sandbox, and the sandbox limit is 30 per minute on v2 as well, which is why your test account fails far sooner than production. Going over either returns RATE_LIMITED with HTTP 429, so size the worker under 600 per minute in production and under 30 per minute in sandbox. Stop ignoring the Retry-After response header, honor it before retrying. For the backlog itself, send each failed delivery through POST /v3/webhooks/deliveries/{id}/retry with the v3 backoff field, which is one of immediate, linear or exponential and defaults to exponential, so the platform spaces the attempts instead of you hammering. Confirm which deliveries are still failed with GET /v3/webhooks/deliveries rather than retrying everything.

ticket.subject: Customers charged twice during a retry storm on the old version, what changed
ticket.body: Post incident review and I need to be able to explain this to our operations lead. Two weeks ago a network blip made our gateway client time out and re authorise the same order, and 61 customers ended up with two live authorisations for the same basket. Our client was already setting a unique per order header value on every attempt and reusing it on the retry, so we assumed the platform would collapse the second attempt into the first. It clearly did not. Our downstream also saw two separate creation messages for the same order, which is how finance spotted it. We are cutting over to the newer version next month and the question I have to answer is whether this can happen again after the cutover, and what our client has to send differently.

outputs.reference_answer: On v2 this is expected behavior. The Idempotency-Key header is optional on POST /v2/payments and a reused key is ignored, so the request is processed again and a second payment is created, which is also why your downstream saw two payment.created events for one order. On v3 it cannot happen the same way, because the Idempotency-Key header is required on every POST /v3/payments request. Sending the same key again with a different request body returns PAY_4090 with HTTP 409, and keys are retained 24 hours, after which the same key may be used for a new payment. So after cutover your client must send an Idempotency-Key on every create and resend the original body unchanged under the same key when retrying.

ticket.subject: Ledger never hears when we release a held authorisation, and I am not sure we are calling the right thing
ticket.body: Our ledger is built entirely off the notification stream and it is drifting. When an order is abandoned before we take the money we release the hold on the card, but the ledger never gets told, so the held amount just sits on our books until someone reconciles by hand. Two questions. First, is there a message type for a released hold at all, because I only see the ones for creation, taking the money and giving it back. Second, one of our engineers wrote the release job and about half the calls come back 422 with PAY_4023 telling us to give the money back instead, which I assume means those orders were not actually abandoned and we had already taken the money on them. So I am no longer confident we are picking the right call for each case. Example is pay_3Kd91xR2.

outputs.reference_answer: There is a message type for it. POST /v3/payments/{id}/reversal releases an authorization that has not been captured and emits the payment.reversed webhook event, which is on the v3 event type list from GET /v3/webhooks/events along with payment.created, payment.confirmed, payment.captured, payment.refunded and payment.failed. Subscribe your ledger to payment.reversed. Your engineer is using the wrong call, because refund returns money on a payment that was already captured while reversal releases one that never was. PAY_4023 with HTTP 422 means the payment was already captured, so use POST /v3/payments/{id}/refund for those and reversal for the genuinely abandoned ones.

ticket.subject: Customer disputing a transaction, need to cancel it before it goes further
ticket.body: We have a customer who is disputing a card transaction and is threatening to raise it with their issuer if we do not sort it out today. I need to cancel the transaction on our side so it does not progress. The payment is pay_3Kd91xR2. Honestly I am not sure exactly what state it is sitting in right now, our internal dashboard just shows it as pending which I do not think maps cleanly onto anything you return. There is also some disagreement here about which version of your API the payments service is actually calling, because the gateway config and the service config do not agree. What call should I be making?

outputs.reference_answer: It depends on whether pay_3Kd91xR2 was ever captured, and that changes the call in both versions. If the money never moved and the authorization is still open, on v2 you cancel it with POST /v2/payments/{id}/void, which marks the payment void so it can no longer be captured, or with POST /v2/payments/{id}/reversal, which releases the full remaining authorization. On v3 the void route is removed and returns 404 for every request, so the equivalent call is POST /v3/payments/{id}/reversal, which releases the uncaptured authorization and emits payment.reversed. If the payment was already captured, cancelling it is a refund rather than a reversal, so call POST /v2/payments/{id}/refund within 30 days of capture on v2 or POST /v3/payments/{id}/refund within 90 days of capture on v3, and a call outside that window returns PAY_4013. Sending a reversal against an already captured payment returns PAY_4023 in both versions, which is the API telling you to refund instead. Your dashboard's pending most likely means authorized but not yet captured, though I cannot confirm that from here. Can you tell me which version the payments service is actually calling, v2 or v3, and whether pay_3Kd91xR2 has been captured yet?

ticket.subject: Nightly settlement report is under-counting and our paging loop stops early
ticket.body: Our nightly settlement report has been off since we moved it onto the new gateway build. The job walks every payment for the previous day and totals them, and the count it prints does not match what treasury reconciles against. Two things look wrong. First, the field the job reads to work out how many pages it needs to fetch is coming back undefined about half the time, so it decides there is one page and stops. Second, when it does keep going, we are seeing the same payment turn up on two different pages and some payments never turn up at all. The person who wrote the loop has left and I cannot get a straight answer internally about what our payments service is pointed at, the config in the repo and what ops say do not line up. How is paging supposed to work here so I can rewrite this properly?

outputs.reference_answer: Paging works two different ways here, and which one you get is exactly what the two symptoms are telling you. On v2, GET /v2/payments uses offset pagination, so you pass offset and limit as query parameters, read total_count from the response to know how many payments match, and the maximum limit is 100. On v3, GET /v3/payments uses cursor pagination, so you pass cursor and limit, follow next_cursor from each response until has_more is false, and there is no total_count field at all, which is why a loop that computes a page count from it would decide there is a single page. The duplicate and missing rows are the classic offset symptom, because payments are returned newest first and new payments arriving mid-run shift every later offset, whereas a cursor is stable across the walk. Note the production rate limit differs too, at 60 requests per minute in v2 and 600 in v3, and paging faster than that returns RATE_LIMITED. Which version is the report actually calling, v2 or v3?

ticket.subject: How far back can we still return money to a customer?
ticket.body: Our complaints team has a backlog of cases where the customer paid a while ago and we have now agreed to give them their money back. Some of these are only a couple of weeks old but a few are getting on for three months since the card was charged. Before I build the queue that processes them I need to know the cutoff, because there is no point queueing something that is going to be rejected and then having to explain to the complaints handler why the customer did not get paid. Is there a hard limit measured from when we took the money, and what comes back if we are past it so I can branch on it cleanly rather than treating every failure the same?

outputs.reference_answer: There is a hard limit and it is measured from capture, but the number depends on which version you call. On v2, POST /v2/payments/{id}/refund allows a refund up to 30 days after capture. On v3, POST /v3/payments/{id}/refund allows up to 90 days after capture. In both versions an attempt after the window returns PAY_4013, a 400 that means the window expired and never means the amount was wrong, which is PAY_4012, so you can branch on that code cleanly. Compare captured_at on the payment against the 30 day or 90 day window before you queue anything, and settle anything outside it outside the payments API. Separately, refunding before the payment.captured event has settled returns PAY_4022, not PAY_4013. Which version is your service calling, v2 or v3?

ticket.subject: Writing signature checks for incoming callbacks, which key am I supposed to use?
ticket.body: I am building the receiver for your callbacks from scratch and I have got to the part where I check the signature on the header before I trust the body. What I cannot work out is which key I am supposed to be computing that signature with. We have a value sitting in the dashboard that looks account wide, and one of my colleagues insists there is a separate key that came back when somebody on the team registered our callback URL months ago and that nobody wrote it down. We have four different URLs registered across our environments, so it matters a lot to me whether one key covers all four or whether each one has its own. Nobody here can tell me which generation of your platform our account is on. What should the receiver be doing?

outputs.reference_answer: Your colleague and the dashboard are both right, just about different versions. On v2, POST /v2/webhooks/endpoints does not accept a secret field at all, and every delivery is signed with the account-level signing secret shared by every endpoint, so the one dashboard value covers all four of your URLs. On v3, secret is required on POST /v3/webhooks/endpoints, and the signing key derived from it is returned exactly once in the create response and never shown again, so each of your four endpoints has its own key and each receiver must verify against that endpoint's key. If you verify with the wrong key the delivery fails with WHK_4220, a 400 signature mismatch, so compute the signature over the exact raw request body before any parsing. If you are on v3 and the key really was never written down, delete that endpoint and register it again to get a fresh signing key. Which version is your account on, v2 or v3?

Right now the only thing I can see is calling the refund route once per payment id, which means four hundred separate requests and a lot of babysitting. Is there a way to hand you a list of payment ids in a single request and have you work through them, ideally with a per item result so I can see which ones failed? I have been through the payments docs and the error tables and cannot find anything that takes more than one id. Before I write the loop and deal with the throttling, can you confirm whether a multi item request exists?

outputs.reference_answer: Our documentation does not describe any way to submit several payment operations in one request, so I cannot confirm whether such a route exists. I do not want to point you at something the reference material does not actually document. Please check with your account contact or our support team before you build around either answer.

ticket.subject: Written availability commitment for our risk review
ticket.body: We are going through third party risk review internally and the reviewers have come back asking for something I cannot produce. They want a written commitment on how available the platform is expected to be, expressed as a percentage over a period, and they want to know your policy on planned maintenance, whether there are announced windows and how much notice we would get before one. This is a sign off blocker for us, so a screenshot of a docs page would settle it. I have searched the payments reference and the error tables and found nothing on either point. Where is this published, and if it is not published, who do I ask?

outputs.reference_answer: Our documentation does not publish an availability commitment or a planned maintenance policy, so there is no page I can point you at. I am not going to state a figure or a notice period that the reference material does not contain. This needs to come from your account contact or our support team in writing so your risk reviewers have something they can rely on.

ticket.subject: Registering and removing a lot of endpoints during a migration
ticket.body: We are moving our receivers to new hostnames next month. That means roughly a hundred and twenty endpoints get registered and the same number get removed, across several environments, in a fairly tight change window. Creating and deleting them one id at a time is a lot of calls to make while a change is in flight and I would rather not be the person hand rolling that script at two in the morning. Is there a way to submit a list of endpoints for creation, or a list of ids for removal, in a single request? I have read the webhooks endpoint pages and the error table and every route I can find takes exactly one endpoint. Wanted to check before I plan the migration around one call per endpoint.

outputs.reference_answer: Our documentation does not cover submitting multiple endpoint registrations or deletions in one request, so I cannot tell you whether that capability exists. Everything published describes single endpoint operations, and I am not going to extrapolate beyond that. Please confirm with your account contact or our support team before you lock in the migration plan.

I want a phone call with our account manager today, and I want it in writing who is accountable for this. Reference on our side is CASE-20988. Do not close this ticket.
